supplement.holds: The main text refers to supplementary data construction (SM S1.1-S1.6), LLM detection and author-level variables (SM S2), event-study and difference-in-differences models (SM S3), and robustness and alternative detection methods (SM S4-S5). The main text reports estimates and P values in the body as well as figures and captions (pp. 3-4, 6, 11-14).

paper_design_summary: The authors apply a text-based LLM detector to abstracts of 2.1M preprints on arXiv, bioRxiv, and SSRN (Jan 2018 to June 2024) and compare authors before and after their first detected LLM use with non-adopters in stacked difference-in-differences event studies. Outcomes are monthly preprint counts, writing complexity (negative Flesch Reading Ease) and its link to publication or ICLR 2024 review scores, and the characteristics of cited references (books, median age, mean log citations). A separate difference-in-differences on 246M arXiv accesses compares Bing-referred with Google-referred users before and after the February 2023 release of Bing Chat. No outcome scores the novelty or creativity of the papers, and no outcome compares outputs across authors for similarity.

studies.label: Author-level event study of LLM adoption on arXiv, bioRxiv, and SSRN (productivity and citation behavior)

participants.who: Preprint authors on arXiv (109,965), bioRxiv (43,218), and SSRN (15,370) tracked Jan 2022 to July 2024 for productivity; manuscripts in core AI subdisciplines excluded (p. 2). The citation analysis links preprints to OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar (101.6M citations, p. 6) and does not state its author count.

eligibility.reason: All four analyses are observational, with no random assignment to AI (pp. 2-7, Results and Limitations and Future Directions). The productivity analysis includes 168,553 authors, meeting the people-count criterion (p. 11, Figure 1 caption); this is an analyzed count, not a randomized count. Outcomes are publication counts, writing complexity, publication/review quality proxies, and characteristics of accessed or cited references (pp. 3-6, Results; pp. 11, 13-14, Figures 1, 3 and 4). None measures creativity, novelty, originality, or similarity/diversity across different authors' outputs. Under creativity-codebook.md sections 3 and 6, the reference characteristics do not qualify as across-people output diversity. The paper is therefore excluded from both the core dataset and observational context.

one_line_finding: LLM adoption, detected from abstract text, is associated with 36.2% (arXiv), 52.9% (bioRxiv), and 59.8% (SSRN) more preprints relative to non-adopters (p. 11, Fig. 1), and adopters cite 11.9% more books, references 0.379 years younger, and references with 2.34% lower citation impact (p. 6; p. 14, Fig. 4), with no measure of the novelty or similarity of the papers themselves.
